styleguide.title: Design reference
styleguide.subtitle: Not a product screen. The tokens and components in one place, with placeholder content rather than sample data.

palette.title: Palette
palette.description: Indigo is the action: it fills the primary button, marks the selected item, and carries the brand. Sky is reserved for sources and citations, and nothing else — a sky chip on screen means the text beside it came from your own material. Emerald is done, amber is due soon, rose is again, overdue, or destructive. Every text/background pair below is checked in both themes by the contrast test, so this list cannot drift from what renders.
palette.contrastNote: Text pairs clear 4.5:1 and borders, icons and the focus ring clear 3:1, in light and dark. The check runs in CI and fails the build on a miss.

swatch.borderStrong: a boundary that must be visible: input edges
swatch.primaryText: indigo as text: links, active nav

type.title: Type
type.body: Body text at 14px on desktop and 16px on mobile. Inter for the interface, Plus Jakarta Sans for headings, JetBrains Mono for page refs and timestamps. All three are bundled, so the app renders with no network.
type.linkAfter: uses the body-text indigo, because the fill indigo is for surfaces that carry white text.

citations.title: Citation marks
citations.description: The identity motif. A mark appears only next to something genuinely traceable, so it never implies grounding that is not there. A mark with a destination is a control; without one it is plain text.
citations.exampleLayer: Encapsulation adds a header at each layer
citations.exampleSeparately: . An outside result is marked separately
citations.interactive: The interactive form is shown above as a web citation, which has a real destination. A chunk citation becomes a button only when a caller passes a handler; with none it renders as text rather than a control that swallows clicks.

controls.title: Controls
controls.descriptionBefore: Appearance only. These are inert samples, not controls: they carry
controls.descriptionAfter: and are outside the tab order, because a button that does nothing is a defect rather than a demo (R-26). A real screen wires each one to its own action.

states.title: States
states.emptyReason: Names why it is empty and what fills it. The reason is a required prop, so a blank state cannot ship by forgetting.
states.errorReason: Names what failed and what to do about it.
states.loading: Loading a named thing, not just loading

course.title: Course colours
course.description: Six categorical hues. Each is a 4px marker plus a tinted chip plus an initial or icon, and never the only signal: two courses in the same colour are told apart by their names, and a course colour is not a status colour.

chips.title: Chips and icons
chips.description: A chip carries a state in words; the tone repeats it, so the state reads correctly in monochrome. Icons are one outline set at 20px, drawn in currentColor so they cannot introduce a colour the contrast check has not measured.

locked.title: Locked features
locked.description: One component, two variants, chosen by the platform. Web and desktop name the plan and link to checkout; iOS and Android state the fact with no price, no button and no link, because the stores review for exactly that.

composer.title: Composer honesty
composer.description: The line under every chat composer, and the grounding toggle above it. Both are part of the composer rather than a tooltip: a warning nobody has to open is one most people never read.

sync.title: Sync status
sync.description: The control the shell shows in both form factors: a row at the foot of the sidebar, and a chip in the tab bar's band on a phone. The state is a word plus a tone, so it reads correctly in monochrome, and the tones are the chips above. It is a link to the Devices screen, which is why Devices needs no sixth nav item.
